title: Biostratigraphic and paleoenvironmental interpretations from Late Pleistocene Ostracoda, Charleston, South Carolina
citation: Lyon, S.K., 1990, Biostratigraphic and paleoenvironmental interpretations from Late Pleistocene Ostracoda, Charleston, South Carolina: U.S. Geological Survey Professional Paper 1367-D, map scale 1:330,000.
notes:
The PDF is the whole Professional Paper 1367 volume (chapters A-G), not only chapter D; this packet covers the volume introduction and the start of chapter A. Table 1 (p. 12) age for Ladson Formation (Q4) is OCR-garbled ('450^00 ka') and was skipped; the Waccamaw(?) Formation (Q6) row is split across table columns and was skipped. Table 2 (p. 32) 14C sample localities are recorded as observations of kind 'other' with the 14C date and material in the note. Units Q1-Q6 are informal units equivalent to named formations (p. 14). Only SC-relevant references from the Introduction list were recorded. The text layer spells Q1 as 'Ql'. Chapter A mineralogy section continues in the next packet.
Packet covers the rest of chapter A (mineralogy, depositional history, tectonics, references) and the start of chapter B (calcareous nannofossils). Heavy-mineral tables 3 and 5-9 (pp. 41-48) and the nannofossil occurrence chart (p. 70) have garbled column headers in the text layer and were not recorded. Unit ages in chapter B (p. 65) differ slightly from Table 1 (p. 12) and chapter A; each is recorded with its own page. Unit Q4 age is about 450 ka in the chapter A abstract (p. 21) but 'probably about 500 ka' on p. 45 and coral ages 'about 500 ka' in the summary (p. 56). Chapter A references: only SC-relevant entries not already recorded from the Introduction list; general references skipped. Chapter B continues in the next packet.
Packet covers the end of chapter B (calcareous nannofossils: unit ages, conclusions, references) and the start of chapter C (Cronin, ostracode evolution). Chapter B unit ages are nannofossil/coral based and differ from ages given elsewhere in the volume; each is recorded with its page. Chapter C tables 3-5 (synonyms, biostratigraphic ranges and evolutionary summary for 127 Atlantic Coastal Plain ostracode species) are region-wide taxonomic data and were not recorded; table 4 column headers are garbled in the text layer. Myrtle Beach area samples (localities 75-81) were not recorded as observations; only Charleston-area samples. Chapter B references: only SC-relevant entries recorded. Chapter C systematic paleontology continues in the next packet.
Packet covers the rest of chapter C (Cronin): table 6 ostracode occurrence chart (pp. 104-111), systematic paleontology, references and plates 1-17, then the title and first page of chapter D (Lyon). Table 6 is a presence/absence chart whose columns are garbled in the text layer; not recorded. Species 'Distribution' lists per formation were not recorded as unit fossils except where a remark characterizes a unit's assemblage. Type localities of new species in South Carolina are recorded as observations (kind 'other') with location exactly as stated; localities repeated for several species are recorded once. The Beaufort quadrangle name is OCR-garbled on p. 115 ('Beaufort ll/z-minute'); the p. 116 instance is cited instead. Chapter C references: only SC- and Atlantic Coastal Plain-relevant entries recorded; general and non-regional references skipped. Chapter D (Lyon) continues in the next packet; its auger holes are described there.
Packet covers chapter D (Lyon) pp. D2-D29: stratigraphic setting, auger holes, biofacies, ecostratigraphy, amino-acid and U-series ages, and the start of systematic paleontology. Auger-hole locations come from table 1 (p. 168), whose columns are interleaved with prose in the text layer; four longitudes (C10, C17, C24, FM3) sit on their own line and were assigned by position. FM1 longitude is printed 70°51'00" (likely misprint), kept as written. C10 and FM2 depths are relative to modern mean sea level, as stated. Figures 3 and 4 (auger-hole columns, occurrence chart) are garbled and not recorded; figure 8 Holocene offshore sample list (p. 182, mostly off Georgia and Florida) not recorded. Species-level stratigraphic ranges and modern occurrences in systematic paleontology not recorded. Systematic paleontology continues in the next packet.
Packet covers the end of chapter D (Lyon) systematic paleontology, its references and plates 1-11, then the title, contents, abstract and first results pages of chapter E (Edwards, dinocysts). Species descriptions, stratigraphic ranges and modern occurrences were not recorded (taxonomic, not unit data); plate captions giving the auger hole and depth of each figured specimen were not recorded. Chapter D references: only SC-relevant entries not already recorded from earlier chapters; general and non-regional references skipped. Chapter E results continue in the next packet (Edisto, Marks Head, Coosawhatchie, Penholoway, Canepatch(?) sections).
Packet covers the rest of chapter E (Edwards, dinocysts: table 1 sample localities, results, references, plates), chapter F (Ward and Blackwelder, Edisto Formation mollusks) and the start of chapter G (Weems and McCartan, fossil occurrences). Chapter E table 1 rows are recorded as observations with sample depth, altitude and location; the state/county/quadrangle columns are partly garbled; sample R3054 is in Chatham County, Ga., and was not recorded as an observation. Sample units come from the text, plate captions, or (R2172A) position in figure 3 (flagged inferred). Figures 1, 3 and 4 of chapter E (zonation chart, range charts) are garbled and not recorded. Chapter G figure 1 ages and symbols recorded per unit; chapter G table 1 (environment/diagenesis), tables 2-3 (diatoms, foraminifers) and table 5 (mollusks) have lost their column alignment in the text layer and were not recorded. Chapter E references are non-SC dinocyst works and were skipped; chapter F references: only SC-relevant entries not already recorded. Species-level systematic paleontology not recorded. Chapter G continues in the next packet.
Packet holds only chapter G of Professional Paper 1367 (Weems and McCartan, fossil occurrences: locality register, references, tables 4 and 6), PDF pages 293-315, plus the series back page. This catalog record is chapter D (Lyon), PDF pages 163-237, so nothing was recorded from this packet.
Scope: this record is chapter D (Lyon) of USGS Professional Paper 1367, PDF pages 163-237 of the whole-volume file. Values read from other chapters' pages were removed from this record; they belong to the other chapters' catalog records.
